1.0 Disclaimer & Important Notices  

 This is a  Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Notice  issued solely for information and market research planning purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10 and DFARS 212.70. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP), solicitation, or promise to issue an award or agreement. 

 The Government will not pay for any information, documentation, or administrative costs incurred in responding to this notice. All costs associated with responding to this RFI are solely at the interested party's expense. 

 Proprietary information, if any, must be clearly marked. The Government will handle proprietary materials in accordance with applicable federal statutes and regulations. 

 Responding to this RFI does not grant any vendor competitive advantage or prejudice any future procurement. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future competitive solicitation or Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) Call that may be issued. 

  2.0 Purpose & Mission Context  

 The USSOCOM Directorate of Procurement (SOF AT&L-K) is conducting market research to determine industry interest and identify commercial partners with  existing, commercially available Enterprise Acquisition Workflow and Super Intelligence Platforms ("Acquisition SI") . 

 Currently, the acquisition environment involves disjointed documents, correspondence, approval routing, authoritative Government systems, and separate artificial intelligence tools. USSOCOM seeks to transition away from fragmented point utilities and prolonged custom software development models by procuring a mature, commercially established platform that natively integrates Super Intelligence across the acquisition lifecycle. 

 The Directorate or Procurement seeks to understand what commercial solutions exist today that can deploy with minimal Government intervention to serve as a common operational workspace for Program Managers, Contracting Officers, Contract Specialists, Agreements Officers, Business Financial Managers (BFMs), and leadership. 

  Key Objective:  The Government is seeking information from commercial software providers capable of delivering a  complete solution  (either as a prime platform vendor or integrated commercial team) rather than disconnected point utilities. This notice signals USSOCOM's interest and benchmarks commercial market maturity across our key operational outcomes. 

  3.0 Core Operational Capabilities of Interest  

 The Government is interested in commercial solutions that currently possess or can readily configure the following capabilities derived from our working Statement of Objectives (Not Attached): 

  Cradle-to-Grave Multi-Pathway Execution:  Managing an acquisition from requirement initiation and planning through document drafting, reviews, award, administration, and closeout across FAR/DFARS contracts and non-FAR instruments (specifically 10 U.S.C. §§ 4021, 4022, and 4023 Other Transactions). 

  Native Super Intelligence Assistance:  Embedded, context-aware AI supporting document development (J&As, PNMs, IGCEs), regulatory compliance grounding (FAR, DFARS, SOFARS 5601, Class Deviations), and administrative checks while strictly preserving human-in-the-loop decision authority. 

  Automated Compliance & PMR Audits:  A dedicated compliance module capable of auditing contract files against agency checklists (such as the Directorate of Procurement DoW PMR Checklist) to support leadership reviews. 

  Natural Language K SharePoint Discovery:  Ability to query internal contract files and SharePoint repositories to locate existing vehicles, past awards, and vetted vendors to avoid duplicative buying. 

  Government Enterprise Interoperability:  Capable of secure data exchange with core acquisition systems (PIEE, SAM.gov, CCaR, Microsoft 365 / SharePoint Online). 

  Open Architecture & Data Portability:  Modular, open API architecture that avoids vendor lock-in, supports model agnosticism (plug-and-play foundation models), and guarantees full data export in standard open formats (JSON, CSV, PDF/A, XML). 

  Cybersecurity & Network Onboarding:  Cloud platform suitable for DoD Impact Level 5 (IL5) operations, willing to actively support the USSOCOM J6 Authorization to Operate (ATO) onboarding process, with an architectural roadmap toward IL6. 

  4.0 Requested Information: Commercial Capability Statement  

 To minimize the burden on industry while providing USSOCOM with actionable market intelligence, interested vendors are requested to submit a concise  Commercial Capability Statement (not to exceed 5 pages)  addressing the following areas: 

   1. Company & Commercial Solution Overview   

 Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, UEI Number, and primary Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email, Phone). 

 Business size status under NAICS 541512 / 513210 and identification of Non-Traditional Defense Contractor (NDC) status pursuant to 10 U.S.C. § 3458 / § 4022. 

 Name and description of your existing commercial platform, commercial availability date, and current operational customer base (specifically across DoD, federal agencies, or enterprise commercial clients). 

   2. Acquisition Lifecycle & AI Capabilities   

  Core Workflow Coverage:  Briefly describe how your commercial platform executes cradle-to-grave acquisition actions. Does your platform currently support both FAR-based contracts and non-FAR Other Transactions (OTs)? 

  Native AI & Regulatory Grounding:  Explain how AI is embedded into daily workflow tasks (e.g., document drafting, compliance verification, and routing). How does the system ensure outputs are grounded in authoritative regulations (FAR/DFARS)?
